Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the team

 

Our Public Services Business Unit is committed to leveraging AI for the benefit of individual citizens and the public good.

From our work informing strategic government decisions, to optimising our NHS, through to reducing bureaucratic backlogs - we know that AI offers opportunities to drive improvements at every level of Government and we are proud to lead on some of the most impactful work happening in the sector.

Because of the nature of the work we do with our Government clients, you may need to be eligible for UK Security Clearance (SC) and willing to work on site with these clients from time to time.

About the role


As a Senior Frontend Engineer at Faculty, you will partner with cross-functional delivery teams in to transform cutting-edge AI and data science models into intuitive, impactful client-facing software.

You will champion modern frontend engineering practices, mentor fellow engineers, and shape our growing frontend community. In this role, you will have the autonomy to solve complex, real-world challenges through elegant interfaces, driving innovation from concept through to deployment in high-stakes environments.

What you'll be doing:

  • Building and scaling resilient, client-facing web applications that bring complex machine learning insights to life.

  • Collaborating closely with data scientists, designers, and engineers across the product lifecycle to design intuitive user experiences.

  • Architecting and maintaining reusable design systems and component libraries to accelerate development across the company.

  • Establishing and maintaining robust CI/CD, development, and deployment workflows alongside modern cloud infrastructure.

  • Championing frontend best practices, engineering standards, and technical excellence across our engineering guilds.

  • Mentoring, onboarding, and supporting team members to foster a supportive and continuous learning environment.

Who we're looking for:

  • You bring strong experience building, testing, and scaling modern web applications using React and modern JavaScript or TypeScript.

  • You have an appreciation for clean component architecture and enjoy developing design systems that work smoothly across multiple platforms.

  • You’re comfortable creating data visualisations using tools such as D3 to make sophisticated insights clear and accessible.

  • You have a solid understanding of frontend build tools (such as Webpack or Babel) and foundational familiarity with backend APIs (such as Node.js).

  • You bring exposure to modern cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and enjoy learning how deployment pipelines fit into the wider software ecosystem.

  • You thrive in an entrepreneurial, collaborative environment where you can share ideas, support peers, and turn complex problems into practical solutions.

Our Interview Process

 

  1. Talent Team Screen (30 minutes)

  2. Pair Programming Interview (90 minutes)

  3. System Design Interview (90 minutes)

  4. Commercial Interview (60 minutes)

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.

A note on AI: we're happy for you to use it for research and interview prep, but please don't use it to generate answers during live interviews. We also use an AI note-taker (Metaview) in interviews so interviewers can stay present (which you can opt out of just let us know,) and every application is reviewed by a human, never decided by AI.

L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès
Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean.

Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 850 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA.

La practice RetailTech regroupe nos clients du retail et de l'e-commerce : des acteurs qui transforment l'expérience d'achat de millions d'utilisateurs, en magasin comme en ligne. Elle rassemble les équipes produit, tech et design qui les accompagnent au quotidien sur des programmes à fort enjeu business.

C'est un domaine en pleine structuration : on y construit la communauté produit, on outille le staffing, on anime les rituels collectifs (all-hands, dojos) et on contribue aux avant-ventes pour faire grandie le portefeuille.

Ton équipe :
Tu rejoindras une communauté tech de plus de 120 Theodoers : software engineers, tech leads, engineering managers et architectes, avec lesquels tu pourras échanger, apprendre et progresser au quotidien.

Chez Theodo, les techs travaillent en équipes projet, constituées en fonction des besoins de chaque client. Tu feras partie d’une équipe de Theodoers à taille humaine (4 à 5 personnes), réunissant Software Engineers, Tech Lead et Product Manager. Ensemble, vous collaborerez étroitement avec le client, avec des échanges réguliers pour partager vos avancées, approfondir la compréhension de son problème et faire évoluer le produit au plus près des besoins de ses utilisateurs.

Tes futures missions :
En tant que Software Engineer Fullstack chez Theodo, ta mission sera de concevoir et développer des produits digitaux utiles, performants et durables pour répondre aux problématiques de nos clients et de leurs utilisateurs.

Tout au long de tes projets, tu seras accompagné pour monter en compétences et apprendre à écrire du code de qualité, à comprendre les enjeux produit et à intervenir sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie d’une application, de la conception au déploiement.

Ce que tu vas apprendre en tant que Software Engineer chez Theodo :


  • Comprendre le problème de ton client et y répondre avec un produit performant, maintenable et orienté valeur, en intervenant sur tout le cycle de production, de la conception au déploiement
  • Produire du code de qualité dans les délais, en intégrant tests, refactoring et standards techniques de l’équipe, quelle que soit la technologie utilisée
  • Mener des investigations techniques, débugger efficacement et corriger les défauts de manière pérenne, dans tout type d’environnement

  • Travailler avec un LLM pour accélérer les développements




Les problématiques et les technos sont très différentes d’un projet à l’autre, voici quelques exemples :

  • iDealwine® : leader mondial des enchères de vins en ligne a engagé la migration de son site e-commerce monolithique vers une architecture composable pour gagner en évolutivité, en sécurité et en maîtrise technologique. Après 2 mois de cadrage, les équipes Theodo ont piloté une approche design-to-cost permettant de modulariser la plateforme et de migrer 20 ans d’historique en 14 mois, dans le respect du budget et du planning
  • Sevetys : refonte complète d’une web app métier avec deux volets stratégiques : un outil de prise de rendez-vous pour les propriétaires d’animaux et un back-office dédié aux vétérinaires. Deux équipes produit ont piloté la reconstruction des plateformes de bout en bout, rejointes en fin de projet par une équipe data pour structurer et valoriser les données. Principal défi : une mise en production coordonnée à grande échelle, impliquant de nombreuses cliniques vétérinaires, sans interruption d’activité

Tes perspectives d'évolution :

Notre Lean Tech® System met l’accent sur l’apprentissage continu : tu évolueras dans un environnement qui investit sur le long terme, où l’objectif est de te permettre de progresser chaque jour, tout en construisant des produits utiles et performants pour nos clients.

industrial clients

connected suppliers

Each Tracklab deployment starts as a SaaS platform implemented within a single industrial company, structuring its compliance and operational data. But the real power comes from what happens next. Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

Our Opportunity

Over the past three years, Predium has built the leading real estate intelligence platform for ESG and value management in the DACH region - with the strongest names in the industry as customers: asset managers, housing companies, banks. Our customer base, our data, our credibility - that's valuable capital for the next step. Investment, credit, and asset management decisions in real estate are still made in Excel, case by case. We're now building the AI analyst that takes this work off people's hands - working directly on the customer's own data, scalable without adding headcount. We're well-funded, and we're bringing AI into real estate.


Your Mission

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you own the systems behind our platform: the GraphQL API, the relational data model, the background processing that turns customer documents and spreadsheets into structured data, and the permission model that lets a single owner and a bank with hundreds of portfolios use the same product. Most of your work runs from schema design all the way to the resolver.
You partner with product, design and other engineers to make sure we build what matters - not just what you have been told to do. You take real responsibility for production: when something is slow, you find out why, whether the answer is a bad query, application code or the infrastructure underneath.
You also help us make AI reliable in production. Document extraction, long-running analysis jobs and agentic features are core to where the product is going, and we need people who make these workflows testable and dependable rather than impressive in a demo.
Our company size of ~40 people ensures that the best idea wins and political discussions are kept aside. And every line of code helps to improve the carbon footprint of real estate properties.

Tech stack: TypeScript (NestJS backend, React frontend), Hasura/GraphQL, PostgreSQL (multiple databases incl. PostGIS), queue-based job processing, AWS (ECS / Elastic Beanstalk, S3, SES, Textract), IaC, Claude but all agents welcome


What you'll own

  • Build features across our Hasura GraphQL API, NestJS and Postgres. From schema design to resolver.
  • Model complex real estate and ESG domains in relational schemas. We run several Postgres databases side by side (one of them geospatial), and schema decisions here have consequences but also positive impact.
  • Own background processing: Excel imports, document extraction, long-running analysis jobs, 3D and image processing. Queues, retries, jobs that spawn other jobs - and figuring out what to do when step 3 of 7 fails at 2am.
  • Develop our permission model. Customers range from a single owner to enterprises with organization/portfolio/building-level access.
  • Integrate LLMs into backend workflows - especially document and data extraction - and make them reliable, verifyable and testable.
  • Debug production. Navigate Grafana dashboards and traces to find out why something is slow or failing, whether in the app, the CI/build pipeline or the infrastructure.
  • Spot overgrown or overly complex parts of the codebase and simplify them without being asked. Paying down complexity is part of the job.


What success looks like

  • You have shipped features end-to-end across schema, API and background processing that our customers actively use.
  • Our async processing (imports, extraction, analysis jobs) is measurably more robust: fewer silent failures, clear retry and recovery paths, and observability that tells us what broke and why.
  • You have taken ownership of at least one core area e.g. the permission model, the job orchestration layer or the LLM extraction pipeline and are the person the team goes to for it.
  • You have raised the bar on testing and developer experience in the backend, and other engineers ship faster because of you.
  • You are a trusted sparring partner for product and the team when we decide what to build and how.


What it takes

  • You're strong with Postgres. Schema design comes naturally, you can read a query plan, and you know when the ORM is lying to you. Geospatial experience is a bonus, not a requirement.
  • You're fluent in typed backend TypeScript. We work in NestJS and GraphQL every day; if your experience is in a comparable stack, that's fine, you'll pick it up fast.
  • You've built real queue-based processing. You designed workers, dealt with retries and partial failures, orchestrated multi-step workflows.
  • You've designed or worked with authorization for a multi-tenant product and know where it might get hairy.
  • You'd rather have one integration test that hits a real database schema than ten unit tests mocking everything. You write the test that catches the broken migration.
  • You treat production as a debuggable system. You can navigate dashboards and traces to figure out why something is slow, and you don't treat infrastructure as someone else's problem.
  • You communicate clearly - with engineers, product and, when needed, directly with customers.
  • You speak German at C1 level or better and English fluently. Our customers are German banks and asset managers, and you will talk to them.
Bonus:

  • AWS (S3, SES, ECS, RDS, …) and IaC.

  • LLMs in production, especially document or data extraction and making it reliable for actual user workflows.

  • Data pipeline work: staged, reproducible processing, dataset versioning.

  • Mentoring or leading engineers, or wanting to grow into it.

  • Debugging tooling and build issues, not just application code. Our toolchain moves fast and is occasionally non-standard.


Why Predium?

  • Stage: ~40 people, well-funded, on the way to defining the category. Early enough that a lot still needs to be built. Yes, it's messy sometimes - that's the whole point. If you're looking for a job with a finished playbook, this isn't the right fit.

  • Impact: You're not cog #100 in some company. What you build here runs in production and is what customers rely on every day. Your contribution shows up directly, in revenue and in the product.

  • Ownership: We don't manage your time, we measure your results. You get responsibility and freedom - and the expectation that you'll use both.

  • Compensation: Competitive salary, bonus, and equity. We want you to share in the success you help create.

  • Team: Office-first in Munich's Werksviertel, 4 days/week.
30 vacation days (including company vacation) · Wellpass · Deutschland-Ticket · Jobrad · team events

We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

A Senior Full-Stack Engineer who owns new features end-to-end: the React interface a clinician clicks, the Python service behind it, and the data model underneath. You have shipped SaaS products inside a high-growth startup, and a slow query bothers you as much as a component that drops frames.

You know where the trade-offs live on both sides of the stack: when logic belongs in the browser and when it belongs on the server, and how a schema decision made today shows up as latency on screen in six months.

You take a loose brief and return a working, tested feature without waiting for a hand-off from another team. You read the user need behind the ticket.

You thrive in a flat, flexible team, and you pick up the specifics of building an AI product for clinicians in 190+ countries within your first weeks.

Brilliant people come from unlikely places. If you have a record of shipping hard, technically demanding products and features, whatever the industry, we want to meet you.

What you'll do

You will work alongside the engineers who built Heidi, shipping AI products that change how healthcare runs.

  • Own features from database to browser: design the data model, build the Python service, ship the React and TypeScript interface, then watch how clinicians use it and iterate.

  • Build fast, accessible interfaces in React, TypeScript and Next.js that hold up for a GP seeing twenty patients before lunch.

  • Design, build and run high-performance backend services in Python, with MongoDB and Redis for storage and caching.

  • Design APIs the rest of engineering and the AI team build on, and own their versioning, documentation, testing and security.

  • Develop and manage message queue systems for real-time data processing.

  • Shape the cloud infrastructure your features run on so they scale and stay up.

  • Pair with product, design and AI engineers to turn a brief into a shipped workflow, then measure and go again.

  • Write code your colleagues can read, test and extend six months from now.

What you'll need

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, with production work on both the frontend and the backend.

  • Strong React and TypeScript, plus Next.js or a comparable framework. You know the browser: rendering performance, state management, accessibility.

  • Python in production: building, testing and running backend services.

  • Hands-on MongoDB and Redis, with sound judgment on data modeling, design patterns and trade-offs.

  • Experience building and managing message queue systems at scale.

  • Deep understanding of API design: security, versioning, performance and the contract between client and server.

  • Application and data security knowledge on both sides of that contract.

  • Experience integrating with third-party systems.

  • Testable, communicative code, and fluency with source control and CI/CD pipelines.

  • A record of building systems that scale, stay up under load and hold up to security scrutiny.

  • Passion for AI, shown through hands-on building, prototyping or side projects.

  • You default to building over requesting.

  • You're confident in your thinking and open to being wrong. Great ideas win regardless of who surfaces them.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.


We take care of you.

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

The team

The Acquisition Tech team owns how iwoca reaches German small businesses – across paid advertising, SEO, social media, direct mail, and outbound sales – and how they become customers. The data and models behind every channel sit with the team.

You'll report to the engineering lead for iwoca's German market, based in London alongside the rest of the technical team. Day to day you'll work with a product manager and a data scientist in London, plus commercial strategy, marketing, and sales – some of whom sit in Germany.

You'll build the backend behind iwoca's German acquisition technology – building on what already runs in the UK, and creating what Germany needs of its own.

  • Ownership. You'll own the German side of the acquisition stack – from the lead-value signals iwoca sends to ad platforms, to the bidding and attribution built on them – and decide what to build from scratch.

  • Technical strategy. You'll help shape the long-term roadmap. The team sets commercial objectives; you’ll shape the architecture, scaling, and technical direction.

  • Funnel optimisation. You'll work with marketing and data science to target relevant businesses across paid search, direct mail, and outbound sales, and to convert more of them once they arrive. You'll integrate third-party APIs to minimise friction in sign-up and improve the lead data behind every channel.

  • Data engineering. You'll build the pipelines, databases, and REST APIs behind the acquisition stack, plus the HubSpot tooling the sales team use.

  • Models in production. You'll engineer the features that data scientists need, put their models into production, and set up the versioning and monitoring that keep them running.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Backend engineering. You have hands-on experience designing and building backend systems in Python, in production.

  • SQL. You are comfortable in SQL beyond CRUD. You shape schemas, tune queries, and reason about how data flows through relational systems.

  • End-to-end. You take work from an initial problem through to delivery, shaping solutions, making trade-offs, and iterating based on how systems are used.

  • Commercial or product thinking. You're comfortable working directly with marketing and sales. You take a business goal, dig into the root of what they need and why, then shape what gets built – as well as owning how.

  • AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Full-stack. You’re open to coding frontend elements, particularly in React or TypeScript.

  • Python stack. You have worked with SQLAlchemy, scikit-learn, pandas, and PostgreSQL.

  • Database design. You have designed, built, and managed relational databases.

  • Analytics tooling. You have used Snowflake, Looker, or the equivalent.

The salary

We expect to pay from £70,000 to £85,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

Le recouvrement de créances est un marché archaïque : 99% des cabinets fonctionnent encore comme dans les années 90. Calls centers massifs, taux de résolution faible, marges écrasées.

Aïstos change ça. Nous avons construit un cabinet de recouvrement hybride où l'IA et l'expertise humaine travaillent ensemble — pas l'un ou l'autre.

Le modèle : l'IA automatise le recouvrement de routine (relances multicanal, scoring, appels) à coût quasi-nul. Les équipes humaines interviennent là où ça compte : litiges complexes, négociation, dossiers sensibles. Résultat : meilleur taux de récupération, coûts divisés par 3, scalabilité sans limite.


Les défis techniques que nous devons résoudre :

  • Orchestrer un workflow intelligent où IA et humain se passent le relais sans friction
  • Bâtir le scoring/routing qui décide automatiquement « IA seule » vs « escalade humaine » (pas d'erreur acceptable)
  • Optimiser l'IA vocale et textuelle pour maximiser les conversions tout en préservant l'empathie
  • Scaler une plateforme qui doit absorber des centaines de milliers de dossiers en parallèle


Stack Technique

  • Backend : TypeScript, Bun, PostgreSQL avec Prisma.
  • APIs : REST & Trpc.

Working closely with designers, engineers, and product managers, you'll take ideas from prototype to production - sweating the animations, haptics, and micro-interactions that make every interaction feel considered, not just functional.   • Design and implement animations and micro-interactions that make every tap feel considered.

  • Fluency in modern JS/TypeScript and cross-platform frontend architecture: performance, accessibility, and scalable UI patterns
  • An eye for interaction design and motion - you know when animations and haptics earn their place and when they're just noise.
